description:
Schloss Dürnstein, the "New Castle", was built between 1622 and 1630 by Christoph Wilhelm of the Barons of Zelking, on the site of an earlier manor and winegrowers' houses; the architect was probably Cipriano Biasino of Krems, who also built the Krems parish church. The hotel's website is the source of this chronology. The palace stands on a rock above the Danube and is a different building from the medieval castle ruin above the town, where Richard the Lionheart was held in 1192–1193.

In 1634 the palace passed by marriage to Heinrich of Zinzendorf and Pottendorf; the Protestant Zinzendorfs left Lower Austria during the Counter-Reformation, and a grandson, Nikolaus Ludwig von Zinzendorf, founded the Herrnhut community. In 1663 it was sold to Conrad Balthasar, Count of Starhemberg; the Starhembergs used it only occasionally, for the vineyards and for hunting. In September 1683 Emperor Leopold I, staying at the castle with a small flotilla on the Danube, received here the news that Vienna had been freed from the Ottoman siege, according to the hotel.

In 1937 Raimund Thiery bought the castle from Ernst Rüdiger von Starhemberg and began converting it into a hotel; his descendants still run it in the third generation. Today it is a seasonal five-star hotel with a terrace restaurant, a spa and indoor and outdoor pools. It stands in Dürnstein, in the Wachau, a UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscape of vineyards along the Danube.
history: Schloss Dürnstein, the "New Castle", was built between 1622 and 1630 for Christoph Wilhelm of Zelking on a rock above the Danube, probably to a design by the Krems architect Cipriano Biasino. In 1634 it passed by marriage to the Zinzendorf family, Protestants who later left Austria during the Counter-Reformation, and in 1663 they sold it to Count Conrad Balthasar of Starhemberg. The Starhembergs used it occasionally for their vineyards and for hunting, and in September 1683 Emperor Leopold I received here the news of the relief of Vienna. In 1937 Raimund Thiery bought it from Ernst Rüdiger von Starhemberg and began turning it into a hotel, which the Thiery family still runs. The palace is a different building from the medieval castle ruin above the town, where Richard the Lionheart was held prisoner.

faqs.question: Is Schloss Dürnstein the castle where Richard the Lionheart was imprisoned?
faqs.answer: No. Richard was held in 1192–1193 in the medieval castle whose ruins stand on the hill above the town. Schloss Dürnstein is a palace built in 1622–1630 on the riverbank below.

faqs.question: Is Hotel Schloss Dürnstein open all year?
faqs.answer: The palace hotel is open from late March to late October. In winter it offers only rooms in an annex and a separate villa, and the restaurant, spa and pools close.

meta_title: Dürnstein Palace, Wachau — Five-Star Palace Hotel on the Danube
meta_description: Stay at Dürnstein Palace on a rock above the Danube in the Wachau, Austria — a seasonal five-star palace hotel with a spa and pools. From approx. €263/night.

hotel.room_location_note: Most rooms are in the palace above the Danube; in winter only rooms in an annex and in a separate villa are offered, so ask the hotel which building your room is in
hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** The hotel is at Dürnstein 2, on a rock above the Danube at the edge of the small town of Dürnstein in the Wachau, about 6 km upstream from Krems an der Donau. Booking lists free private parking with valet service and electric charging, and notes train access.

**Rooms & rates:** From approx. €263/night for a 20 m² Double Room with a queen bed on a non-refundable rate that can be rescheduled, with breakfast at about €30 extra; a free-cancellation rate was around €299, and the same room with breakfast included around €314. Booking showed the price with taxes and fees included, plus a possible member discount that is not included here.

**On-site:** A terrace restaurant above the Danube, a spa, indoor and outdoor pools, a bar and a library, free parking and free Wi-Fi.

**Good to know:** The palace hotel is seasonal: in 2026 it opened on 27 March and closed on 26 October, and in winter only rooms in an annex and a separate villa are offered, with the restaurant, spa and pools closed. Rates were seen for one early-April 2027 night, at the start of the season, so check your own dates on Booking. The terrace restaurant is also open to non-guests during the season.

**Combine with:** [Dürnstein Castle](/castles/austria/durnstein-castle), the ruined medieval castle above the town where Richard the Lionheart was held, and [Aggstein Castle](/castles/austria/aggstein-castle), further up the Wachau.
